summary: Weekly POC sync focused on Dedicated capacity sizing and governance. Redwood reviewed autoscale windows, pre-warm options and cost guardrails; Synapse raised concerns about unpredictable surge billing and KMS integration for PHI. Agreed to run controlled bursts and share telemetry to finalize commit sizing.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-01-12 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~52m | Attendees: Maya, Jon (Redwood) -- Priya, Marco, Lena (SynapseHealth)

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, hope you all had a good week. Today we're going to zero in on the dedicated sizing ask and the governance around burst and pre-warm. Jon from infra will walk through the test plan.

[00:28] Jon (SE): Hi all. Quick agenda: review last week's run, propose autoscale windows, show pre-warm options (instant vs queued), then map to cost impact. I have the results slide deck here: https://redwood.example.com/poc/synapse/benchmark-deck

[00:52] Priya (Eng Mgr): Quick context — our production has spiky traffic, sometimes 10x baseline for 20-30 minutes, and if we go with hosted we need clear caps. We also have PHI concerns so KMS + audit logs are non-negotiable.

[01:15] Marco (SRE): Also we run nightly batch jobs that touch the same models, so KV cache behavior during bursts is important, we saw cache thrash in the last sim which bumped latencies.

[01:40] Jon (SE): Right, so two takeaways from last run: 1) with baseline of 4 Dedicated units and autoscale up to 12 we saw tail latencies at 95th of ~420ms for 1k concurrent users; 2) when a sudden 3x surge hit, cold start caused a 2.3x token cost bump because kernels recompiled and KV missed. Note — some of the log labels in the run had the model name spelled "redwood-dediate-v1" in telemetry, small transcription in the logs.

[02:20] Lena (Product): Are we able to pin a warm pool that survives for X minutes? Our compliance team wants determinism.

[02:37] Jon (SE): Yes, pre-warm pool with configurable TTL — options: keep-warm (minutes) or keep-warm-on-traffic (adaptive). Keep-warm adds fixed hourly cost; pre-warm-on-demand has a small per-burst ramp fee. We showed the math on slides 6-8.

[03:00] Priya (Eng Mgr): Concern is opaque surge cost. If your autoscaler spins up GPUs and we get charged per token at higher rate, how do we cap that?

[03:18] Maya (AE): Good point — we recommend committed burst units as part of the Dedicated contract. That caps per-burst rates and gives predictable invoicing; after committed burst is exhausted there's a throttled fallback and a notification policy.

[03:44] Marco (SRE): Can we set hard budget caps or a fail-open to lower-tier model to avoid runaway cost?

[03:52] Jon (SE): Yes, two mechanisms: budget guardrail (hard stop) and graceful fallback to smaller model variant. Also route-by-policy so latency-critical paths prefer pre-warm nodes.

[04:10] Priya: And KMS? We need to know if keys stay in our HSM and whether the audit logs capture per-token access.

[04:22] Maya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and per-request audit logs. We'll share SOC2 + KMS integration docs after this call.

[04:40] Jon: For the upcoming controlled burst test — plan is: 2-hour window, step up concurrency 1x -> 3x -> 5x at 20 minute intervals, include KV cache warm and cold variants. We'll collect latency, token rate, pre-warm hit rate, OOM events.

[05:05] Marco: How will you simulate our prompt distribution? Our average prompt length is variable, around 120 tokens but long tails to 1k.

[05:19] Jon: Please send us the histogram CSV (top 100) and we'll seed the generator. If you can't share real prompts because PHI, provide anonymized token-length distribution.

[05:35] Priya: We'll anonymize and share by Friday.

[05:40] Maya: Cost calc — for a 3x sustained burst with pre-warm pool set to 30 minutes, estimated incremental monthly cost is shown on slide 9. There's also a burst add-on that gives discounted pre-warm rate.

[06:05] Lena: What's the SLA impact if we fallback to smaller model?

[06:15] Jon: Latency increases roughly 30-60ms depending on model. Quality regressions are minimal for our reranker style prompts but for critical flows we'd prefer to avoid fallback. We can add canary routing — only non-critical traffic falls back.

[06:45] Marco: Operationally, I want a single place to see token spend by route and a signal when pre-warm is consumed. Does console do token-level tracing?

[06:57] Maya: Yes — Redwood Console gives per-route token and latency breakdowns with a threshold alerting UI. We'll set up a dashboard for Synapse pilot.

[07:15] Priya: On retention and cache: if we evict KV cache after X minutes we saw cold starts in the last sim. Can we make eviction policy sticky for named tenants?

[07:30] Jon: Tenant pinning for KV is supported in Dedicated. You can set tenant-specific TTL and pin certain keys — useful for low-churn prompts.

[07:48] Priya: Great. For compliance, can we prove deletion and data residency per request?

[07:55] Maya: Audit logs + request-level metadata recorded, with optional longer retention for enterprise. We'll include retention SLAs in the Private contract.

[08:10] (short crosstalk) Marco: timestamps in logs are slightly skewed in last run (clock drift) — we'll ensure NTP sync before next test.

[08:32] Jon: On autoscale windows, recommendation is: keep a warm baseline sized to 95th of typical traffic, autoscale headroom of 2-3x for normal surges, and define an emergency burst pool for 5x spikes (pre-warmed at low cost). We'll show policy YAML after call.

[08:58] Priya: Can you show the policy examples?

[09:05] Jon: Sure. Example snippet: scalePolicy: {type: "incremental", step: 2, coolDownSeconds: 120}. Apologies if transcription mangles brackets. We'll push the real YAML to the shared folder.

[09:28] Lena: Any thoughts on multi-region? Our users are global and a regional outage is a risk.

[09:37] Maya: Multi-region routing is supported. We recommend primary in us-east-1 + failover replica in eu-west-1 for latency-sensitive endpoints. Cross-region cache warming can be expensive — better to replicate model weights and warm separate pools.

[10:05] Priya: Ok. Last week's run indicated a weird spike in tokenization time — could be tokenizer implementation mismatch.

[10:18] Jon: We'll validate tokenizer versioning in the runtime and include the exact model+tokenizer hash in telemetry. Expect that in the run logs.

[10:35] (silence)

[10:47] Maya: Recap of decisions: run controlled 2-hour burst, Redwood shares pricing variants with committed burst units and pre-warm add-on, Synapse shares traffic histogram and KMS details. We'll aim to finalize commit sizing after the run.

[11:12] Marco: One operational ask — can Redwood surface estimated bill impact in real-time so we can abort a test if cost delta exceeds X%?

[11:24] Jon: Yes, we'll enable a live estimate feed in the dashboard for the test run. It hooks into the same accounting pipeline.

[11:35] Priya: Thanks — that helps. Any blockers on Redwood side?

[11:40] Maya: None, just need the histogram and KMS provider. We'll also need a short window to run the dry run; Marco and Jon to coordinate via Slack.

[11:55] Lena: Let's schedule the engineering dry-run early next week.

[12:05] Maya: Great — we'll follow up with invite. Thanks everyone.

[12:15] (meeting ended)
notes: Redwood to provide YAML policy examples and pricing variants
